In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in a minority of cases, KRAS mutational changes occur during the course of CRC and that this is not necessarily associated with a change of histology.
the observed KRAS status changes in recurrent tumors and metastases are most probably not due to tumor progression but to multiple tumor formation in the same patients.
the observed differences in the KRAS mutational profile may be caused by tumor heterogeneity, progression or even multiple tumor formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the case of colorectal cancer, the KRAS mutation status is not stable and may be changed during the course of the disease.
in a significant number of CRC patients with recurrent tumors or metastasis the KRAS status may differ from the primary tumor.
KRAS mutational analysis in CRC patients should be performed in all available tumor samples to avoid false-negative or false-positive results.
The main takeaway from our work is that
KRAS mutational analysis in recurrent CRC should be performed in order to avoid the use of targeted therapies in cases with wild-type KRAS.
the analysis of KRAS mutations in colorectal tumors is a complex process that should be performed with great caution and in a large series of cases.
